title: New York unveils advanced nuclear master plan
html:
The plan, which was co-authored by the New York State Energy Research Development Authority and the New York State Department of Public Service outlines coordinated state actions to support the safe and timely development and deployment of advanced nuclear power plants in upstate New York. It was issued alongside a DPS White Paper with policy recommendations to support the commercial viability of the project and potential cost reductions.

The master plan was developed in response to Hochul’s 2025 directive to establish a framework supporting advanced nuclear energy development in New York. It aims to facilitate the plans for 5 GWe of new nuclear generation in Upstate New York under the Nuclear Reliability Backbone initiative unveiled by the governor in her annual State of the State address in January. This is in addition to the 3.4 GWe of nuclear capacity already in existence in the state.

"Expanding emission-free, round-the-clock nuclear power is a cornerstone of my all-of-the-above approach to ensure we have enough energy to keep the lights on and costs down for New Yorkers," Hochul said. "The completed Advanced Nuclear Master Plan can serve as a national model by pairing our ambitious target of five gigawatts of new nuclear generation with a comprehensive strategy to support thoughtful development and deployment of what will be the largest buildout the country has seen in more than three decades."

The 30-point Master Plan, which is supported by 12 studies and more than 1,000 pages of research and analysis, identifies New York State actions to further assist with responsible advanced nuclear development. Areas of focus identified in the plan to support responsible advanced nuclear development include, amongst other things, advancing a policy framework to support deployment; capitalising on investments and building on federal investments and opportunities, such as the US Army's plans to site a microreactor at Fort Drum under the Janus Project; maximise nuclear supply chain opportunities, including setting up a nuclear supplier readiness programme; building the workforce for nuclear energy; identifying potential sites and partnering with communities to prepare for development; and adapting state regulatory processes while maintaining "uncompromising" safety.

The Master Plan calls for a process to identify interested host communities, evaluate suitable sites, including brownfields, and support early site characterisation and evaluation.

Hochul's announcement came the day after the New York Power Authority named the ten nuclear energy developers it has qualified to go forward in its process to select potential partners for its effort to develop at least 1 GWe of advanced nuclear power capacity in Upstate New York, following a Request for Qualifications issued in May.
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul has announced the completion of the Master Plan for Responsible Advanced Nuclear Development in New York, which sets out a roadmap for the state to achieve its target of creating 5 GW of new nuclear power capacity.
